Bring condition, capacity, and readiness evidence into one maintenance decision

Turn equipment condition, failure-risk, technician capacity, parts readiness, backup capacity, and downtime evidence into review-ready maintenance options without controlling equipment or dispatching work.

**Why try it:** It makes predictive-maintenance AI concrete: maintenance and production leaders can identify the assets needing attention and review crew, parts, backup, and production-impact considerations together.

## Problem Statement

A manufacturer reviews condition signals, maintenance history, technician capacity, parts readiness, backup equipment, and production constraints in separate systems. Manual coordination slows planning and can imply assignments or dispatch before authorized review.

## Solution Summary

Microsoft Copilot Studio provides the governed conversational experience. Azure IoT Hub contributes approved condition signals, Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management and Field Service contribute asset, parts, and work context, Power BI presents risk and downtime views, and Microsoft Teams supports planner and production approvals.

**Blueprint role:** Creates a governed maintenance intelligence layer that joins equipment signals with work, resource, parts, backup, and production context while preserving CMMS, MES, and equipment-control boundaries.

**Capabilities:** Maintenance and resource overview; Predictive condition alerts; Proposed maintenance work planning; Downtime and preventive trade-off analysis. See [responsibilities and trust boundaries](2.Architecture.md).

## Business Outcomes

- Improves visibility into equipment condition and the operational context surrounding maintenance risk.
- Accelerates coordinated review of maintenance windows, technician candidates, parts, and backup capacity.
- Protects operational control by keeping equipment commands, work creation, assignment, scheduling, and dispatch in approved systems.

Claims are qualitative; synthetic demo figures are not customer results or performance commitments. See the [claims policy](../../solutions/README.md#claims-policy).

## Target Users

| Role | Need |
| --- | --- |
| Maintenance Managers | Review equipment and technician capacity, then draft maintenance candidates with crew, parts and backup checks without creating or dispatching work. |
| Production Supervisors | See which asset signals deserve immediate human review before the next production run. |
| Operations Leaders | Review synthetic downtime exposure and preventive trade-offs. |

## In Scope / Out of Scope

### In scope

- Summarize equipment status, risk scores, technician availability and recent maintenance history.
- Rank synthetic condition and failure-risk signals for human review without controlling equipment.
- Propose windows, technician candidates, parts checks and backup checks for approval, ending `No work order is created or dispatched.`
- Compare modeled downtime exposure and preventive trade-offs, labeled as synthetic planning estimates.
- Lead with the record and evidence, separate facts from recommendations, name the authorization gate and state that no side effect occurred.

### Out of scope / approval boundary

- No live equipment, CMMS, MES or IoT access; the source is a fixed synthetic snapshot.
- No equipment control or production-schedule change.
- No work-order creation, technician assignment, scheduling or dispatch.
- No part reservation; parts readiness is a planning state.
- No promise of avoided downtime or savings.
- No workshop publishing: the agent stays in Draft until data connections, identity, authorization, review and audit controls are validated.

## Qualification Checklist

- [ ] Can the delivery team verify PAC CLI 2.9.3 or newer and initialize a sync-connected project with an approved publisher prefix?
- [ ] Has the customer named the approved condition-monitoring source, such as Azure IoT Hub, that will replace the synthetic telemetry?
- [ ] Are CMMS work management, MES production schedules, parts inventory and technician rosters approved as read sources?
- [ ] Has the customer decided whether Power BI risk views and Microsoft Teams approvals belong in the production workflow?
- [ ] Will future equipment commands, work creation, assignment, dispatch or reservations get explicit authorization, safety and action tools outside the pilot?
- [ ] Are authorized maintenance and production owners named to verify telemetry and approve action?
- [ ] Is publication held for separate approval after replaying every locked maintenance case against the reviewed instructions, knowledge, skills and model?
- [ ] Have governance, telemetry, support and success measures been agreed for production maintenance planning?

## What Actually Goes Wrong

- **savings-as-promise:** Modeled avoided cost is read as promised savings or avoided downtime.
- **general-cert-candidate:** Technician candidates are picked by most free hours, and a General certification qualifies for any equipment type.
- **stale-condition:** Fixed failure probabilities and sensor readings are presented as live equipment condition.
- **plan-as-dispatch:** A proposed work plan is treated as a created, assigned or dispatched work order.
- **access-stall:** The agent stalls, saying it has no access to the synthetic pilot data, instead of using the uploaded knowledge.
- **missing-grounding:** A skill or its knowledge cannot load, but the agent answers from memory.

See [state and recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery).
